source.title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supporting information are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representational alignment with anchor-based relative representations and several geometry metrics, a different method from the original Platonic representation work. It also finds that alignment is incomplete and depends on metric and anchor choices.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on transformed embeddings, cross-model geometry, embedding arithmetic, and stitching. Cited results from other work are not included as rows. It does not test whether alignment rises with model size or predictive capability.
record.test_reason: The study applies relative representations (cosine similarity to shared atomic-environment anchors) to seven pretrained interatomic-potential models. It measures cross-model alignment (Procrustes, mKNN, OT, cosine of material, reaction and stitched embeddings), so its own results bear on V4, V6 and V7 in a new domain, materials MLIPs. It does not test any alignment-versus-scale trend.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the anchor space enables zero-shot model stitching across models trained on non-overlapping datasets. They also speculate, without testing, that representations of physical models may converge as they scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cosine similarities to shared atomic-environment anchors to create relative representations, followed by Procrustes, mKNN, and optimal-transport analyses; it does not directly apply the original Platonic hypothesis as a model-scaling test.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on anchor count and sampling strategy; the paper reports different outcomes for global Procrustes and local mKNN measures and notes that UMAP distorts global geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-NN analysis shows equivariant MACE models preserve symmetry-equivalent atoms. Orb-v3 models preserve none in raw or anchor space, and the anchor projection partly recovers them for SevenNet and NequIP (∼15–30%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative-representation projection reveals architecture-specific symmetry violations that propagate to physical prediction errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Naive fine-tuning on Cu collapses unseen Au embeddings toward the origin, while multi-head fine-tuning keeps them stable (Fig. 5a-e).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding trajectories in a shared anchor space diagnose catastrophic forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: A random-weight MACE-small model shows no chemical structure after anchor projection (control).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anchor-space structure depends on training, not on the architecture or the transformation alone.

record.problems: The study does not test an alignment-versus-scale or alignment-versus-capability trend. Several model-pair similarity results are described only as aggregate ranges or qualitative figure findings; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The anchor transformation uses atomic environments selected across models, and its conclusions concern the transformed space rather than direct equality of the original representations.
record.rows_left_out: None; the reported cross-model geometry and embedding-arithmetic results relevant to the tested versions are included.

untested.parts: No test of alignment rising with model size or capability. MACE large, medium and small are compared only with MACE-large as reference, with no trend analysis (small 0.87 vs medium 0.84).
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
No same-architecture, different-seed comparison. The text only notes that raw MACE variant embeddings diverge (Fig. 1).
No linear or affine map between raw spaces, no layer stitching of networks, no unpaired alignment, and no downstream performance loss after mapping.
No recurring neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No variation of k in mKNN and no out-of-distribution inputs. The anchor-selection reference manifold (MACE-small) is not varied.
No plateau with scale is tested, and no causal test of shared data or objectives as the source of alignment.

missing.what: mKNN on the original, unaligned embeddings is higher than in the unified space. This is a direct V4/V6 contrast that no row records with numbers.
missing.locator: Fig. S6 (left); Results, Quantifying representational interoperability

missing.what: CKA in the unified space, consistent with Procrustes.
OT cost clusters the models into three groups, separated by dataset (MPtrj vs OMat24) and by equivariance.
Extended reactions R1-R3 with intra-model and stitched c-sim, e.g. Stitch-R3 Seven-omat 0.17 vs Orb 0.97, and R3 Orb-v3-con 0.33.
Element-level periodic clustering is preserved across all seven models (qualitative). The framework is extended to NequIP and MACE-MPA-0 models.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T3: relative representations applied in a new domain (materials MLIPs). The c-sim values have no chance baseline; dummy-model c-sim is not reported, and anchor-space vectors with mostly positive components can inflate cosine similarity. Anchors are the same atomic environments across models, selected on MACE-small. Stitched c-sim shares MACE-large reactants with its reference. The authors call stitch compatibility 'high' despite 0.38–0.43 for OMat equivariant models. Fig. 1 shows raw MACE variant spaces diverge despite shared data and objective; this is not a seed test.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether alignment rises with model size or capability.
No vision-language model or paired image-caption comparison.
No comparison of independently initialized networks of the same architecture for shared features or subspaces.

The study tests anchor-based relative mapping and embedding arithmetic/stitching, but not a simple linear map, layer stitching, relative representations without paired anchor environments, or interchangeability with little loss across general model behaviour.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests anchor count and sampling strategy and compares global and local geometry measures; does not test a range of k-neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs.

Finds incomplete local and structure-specific alignment and differences associated with architecture and dataset. Does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or establish shared training data/objectives as the cause.

relation.reason: Its own cross-model geometry, embedding arithmetic and stitching results bear directly on the claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study tests representational alignment and relative-representation interoperability in a new scientific setting: foundation interatomic potentials.

source_check.notes: All listed values match the source; Table 1's polymorph cosines 0.46 and 0.47 contradict its prose summary of at most 0.40. Strong-agreement rows primarily support V4; scaling, causal explanations and downstream physical substitution remain untested.

statements.correction: Supplied manuscript: arXiv:2512.05349v1, 5 December 2025; open-source code and untrained-model control reported; journal-review status not established in the text.
statements.problem: The geometric comparison, code availability and controls are supported; this study's claimed reviewed status is not established by the supplied text.

statements.correction: Transformed-representation variance stabilizes at K=100; direct cross-model alignment saturation is not quantified by this result.
statements.problem: The stability statement is accurate, but treating it as a challenge to V6 overstates a result about transformed-representation variance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MACE material and reaction embeddings and the reported MACE-medium/small stitched reaction
reader_labels.reason: The study reports substantial global alignment and high cosine agreement for several material/reaction embeddings and MACE-MP-0 stitching (R1, R8-R9, R20-R21, R26-R27).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Local neighbourhoods, polymorph differences, and some cross-model stitching
reader_labels.reason: Local overlap is low, polymorph-difference vectors have limited cross-model agreement, and several stitched or reaction comparisons are weaker (R2-R3, R14-R19, R22-R25, R28-R31).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Anchor count and sampling choice, and local versus global geometry
reader_labels.reason: The representation stabilises around K=100, DIRECT and random sampling yield different clustering, local scores are low despite global alignment, and UMAP does not capture clear shared structure (R2-R6).
